findings.claim: Step 4 of the how-to says the quoted workflow is ci.yml's knowledge job with actions/checkout 'at its version tag instead of a commit SHA'. ci.yml pins checkout at v7.0.1, but the quoted block uses actions/checkout@v4, so a reader takes v4 to be the tag of the shipped pin, which is false. Say what the block actually uses (for example 'actions/checkout@v4 instead of the pinned commit SHA'), and keep the block's content unchanged as the plan asks.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan asks.

ci.yml runs on every pull request and every push to main, with three jobs: knowledge (`uses: ./` after a full-history checkout), prek (`uvx prek@0.5.5 run --all-files`, the version the justfile pins) and tests (`uv run pytest`, the default tier).
Actions are pinned by SHA with version comments that match release-tag.yml, and setup-uv runs with its cache off.
knowledge.yml is deleted, and the how-to now cites ci.yml's knowledge job.
One wording slip in the how-to remains (f1).
It does not block.
Read the diff in full: the staged deletion of knowledge.yml, the unstaged how-to edit, and the untracked ci.yml and tests/test_ci.py.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format, tests and integration pass, rows r1 to r7 pass, "stamp green: b906426ff5ba39ed32b3f9e8a38010f620038eddd8a233e7985e25f0107cfeaf".
`uvx prek@0.5.5 run --all-files` passes and leaves the tree unchanged.
`kmctl check` on the worktree prints "all checks passed".
Eval rows, test by test.
r1 asserts `pull_request` in `on` and `push.branches == ["main"]`.
r2 finds the job whose steps contain `{uses: ./}` and asserts that its checkout has `fetch-depth: 0`.
A missing key raises, which fails the test.
r3 reads the version from the justfile and asserts the exact run line.
r4 asserts that the only pytest run line is exactly `uv run pytest`, so adding `-m` fails it.
r5 asserts that every non-local `uses` is owner/repo@40-hex and that every setup-uv step has `enable-cache` set to False.
r6 asserts that knowledge.yml is absent.
r7 extracts the "quoted from" note and the step 4 "This is ..." sentence and checks that every `.github/workflows/` path in them exists.
I ran its regexes by hand: the step 4 capture ends at "`uses" but still contains the ci.yml path, so changing that sentence back to knowledge.yml would fail the row.
Each `-k` selector picks at least one test, because pytest exits 5 when it selects none.
Consistency: the pyproject marker description says the integration gate in .loop/config.toml runs the integration tier, which matches the comment on the tests job.
grep outside .loop/ finds no other reference to knowledge.yml besides the how-to's instruction to create one in the user's own repo, which the plan keeps as is.
f1: the step 4 sentence says checkout is "at its version tag", but the quoted block uses @v4 while ci.yml pins v7.0.1.
The fix is a wording change, so it does not need another round.
prek's `--all-files` covers tracked files only, so it did not check ci.yml and tests/test_ci.py while they are untracked.
The ruff gates cover the test file, and the YAML parses in the tests.
